{"id": "ad145bd8-079a-4973-868f-31fd25b44fe7", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Good instinct to isolate it that way — the evidence does point away from DynamoDB's own processing, but I'd narrow the conclusion a bit before calling it a "client-side" problem.

**What the signals tell you:**
- GetItem/PutItem p50 and p99 matching 7-day baselines, p99 under 15 ms, with normal volume → DynamoDB is processing requests at normal speed once they arrive at the service.
- No SystemErrors, no throttling → DynamoDB isn't rejecting or internally erroring on requests for either operation.

That combination effectively rules out the DynamoDB service itself (partition hot-spotting, internal errors, throttling, capacity issues) as the cause in this window.

**Why "client side" isn't quite the right scope:**
DynamoDB's p50/p99 only measure time spent *inside* DynamoDB processing a request it has received. They say nothing about everything that happens before that: DNS resolution, TCP/TLS handshake, routing between the two VPCs, NAT gateways, VPC peering/Transit Gateway hops, or whether that other VPC even has a DynamoDB VPC endpoint (if not, traffic may be taking a longer path out through an IGW/NAT instead of PrivateLink). An 800 ms call with occasional timeouts, while DynamoDB itself answers in single-digit milliseconds, is the classic signature of latency being added in that network path — not necessarily in the client application code.

It could also be client-side in the narrower sense — connection pool exhaustion, lack of connection reuse/keep-alive, thread starvation, or aggressive retry/backoff config — which would also show up as "slow calls" without DynamoDB itself seeing anything wrong.

So the fair classification is: **the problem is outside DynamoDB's server-side processing — somewhere between the client and the DynamoDB endpoint**, and that could be either network path/VPC connectivity or the client's own connection handling. I wouldn't commit to "client side" specifically without checking the VPC endpoint configuration and connection-level behavior (e.g., TCP retransmits, connection setup time vs. request time) on that other VPC's side.

If you want, I can look into whether that VPC has a DynamoDB VPC endpoint configured, or dig into connection-level timing — just let me know which.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
